adds.quote: In order to provide values for the decision rule variables, we introduce a set of rationality relations R = {rD }D∈D that describe assumptions about how the agents choose decision rules.
adds.formula: mM=(m\mathcal G,\theta,R),\quad m\mathcal G=(N,\mathbf V\cup\mathbf M,m\mathcal E),\quad m\mathcal E:=\mathcal E\cup\{(M_V,V)\}_{V\in\mathbf V}\cup\mathcal E',\quad \mathcal E'\subseteq\bigcup_{D\in\mathbf D}(\mathbf M\setminus\Pi_D)\times\Pi_D,\quad r_D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}(\mathbf{Pa}_{\Pi_D})\times\operatorname{dom}(\Pi_D)\text{ serial};\qquad \text{e.g. }\pi_D\in r^{BR}_D(\mathbf{pa}_{\Pi_D})\iff\pi_D\in\arg\max_{\hat\pi_D\in\operatorname{dom}(\Pi_D)}\sum_{U\in\mathbf U^i}\mathbb E_{(\hat\pi_D,\pi_{-D})}[U].
adds.assumptions: A MAID with known parameters (common prior); mechanism variables Θ_V for parameters and Π_D for decision rules; rationality relations (e.g. best response) stating how each agent picks its rule given the other mechanism variables. The mechanised graph may be cyclic.
adds.gloss: Adds a variable for each parameter and decision rule, plus relations saying how agents choose rules, so interventions can propagate into the agents' policy choices.
adds.relation: Substrate for Pre-policy interventions and for the rational outcomes over which Interventional query and Counterfactual query in games quantify; plays the role that the policy oracle plays in Ward et al. (2024).
